h: פָּרָשַׁת כִּי תָבוֹא, ט״ז Ki Savo, 16
Israel’s Holiness Endures Through Blessing Rebuke and Exile

p: "And all these blessings shall come upon you
Our Rebbe of Izhbitz, of blessed memory,
said that the meaning of "and overtake you" is
for sometimes a person can change
Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
And likewise one may say further on, regarding the opposite,
וּבָאוּ עָלֶיךָ כָּל וְגוֹמֵר וְהִשִּׂיגוּךָ (שָׁם כח, טו)
"and all … shall come upon you, etc., and overtake you" (ibid. 28:15).
of the reward and punishment of the mitzvos,
for this is not in this world,
and tomorrow to receive their reward"
but rather the blessings of this world,
that is, that Hashem will give all the assistance
so that one can serve Hashem with greater vigor.
And if, Heaven forfend, they do not listen,
so that thereby they will take to heart
to return and improve their ways.
on the day of the destruction,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נוֹלַד תֵּיכֶף מָשִׁיחַ
and thereby Mashiach was immediately born
(as written in Midrash Rabbah, Eichah, and elsewhere).
And likewise the Keruvim immediately turned
their faces each toward the other,
when Yisrael do the will of the Omnipresent
And for this reason it is brought (Yoma 54b):
in resolving the question of the Ritva).
and they went down into exile,
that the yetzer hara would rule
and they would be assimilated among the nations;
"and all … shall come upon you, etc.";
that you will not change from the hour of the destruction,
and all this will be assistance
so that they merit to rectify everything completely.
the Name Havayah is mentioned eighteen times
and the eighteenth time it is written,
"And Hashem will bring you back to Egypt in ships,
by the way of which I said to you,
לֹא תוֹסִיף עוֹד לִרְאוֹתָהּ (דְּבָרִים כח, סח)
which the Zohar Chadash (on this parshah) explains
that the Holy One, blessed be He, performed in Egypt,
'As in the days of your going out of Egypt
I will show him wonders' (Michah 7:15), etc."
And it expounds a gezeirah shavah of "in ships"
מִמַּה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר בָּאֳנִיּוֹת רִנָּתָם (יְשַׁעְיָה מג, יד)
from what is said, "in the ships of their song" (Yeshayahu 43:14):
just as there it is song,
so here too it is song.
And as for what is said,
"by the way of which I said to you,
it appears that the Zohar Chadash explains:
just as they were promised at the Exodus,
so then, at the time of the redemption,
all the nations of the world will perish,
and you will see them no more;
of the redemption and the salvation.
"And Hashem will bring you back, etc."
that He will return our dispersed,
in which it is mentioned that Hashem will do,
which is the numerical value of "tov," good;
because in truth there is hidden in them
that Hashem will do at the end of days.
אִמְרוּ צַדִּיק כִּי טוֹב (יְשַׁעְיָה ג, י)
"Say of the tzaddik that he is good" (Yeshayahu 3:10)
That is, according to what was written by
that the main purpose of the last exile
is for the rectification of the blemish of the covenant,
And therefore there came seventeen expressions
that Hashem will bring the opposite,
they will merit to rectify the attribute of tzaddik, Yesod;
to which the number tov alludes,
And the passage of rebuke opens
and as for what is said,
וְהָיָה כַּאֲשֶׁר נִלְכְּדָה יְרוּשָׁלָיִם (יִרְמְיָה לח, כח)
"And it came to pass when Yerushalayim was captured" (Yirmiyahu 38:28),
for on that day Yisrael received the final verdict
וְכָאן הוּא גַּם כֵּן לְשׁוֹן שִׂמְחָה
And here too it is an expression of joy,
they will merit to return in teshuvah
as it was before the damage.
And it says first ten expressions
מִן הַפָּסוּק יְשַׁלַּח ה׳ וְגוֹמֵר (שָׁם כח, כ)
from the pasuk "Hashem will send, etc." (Devarim 28:20);
and this corresponds to the ten attributes:
that is, that they will rectify
all that they damaged in the ten attributes,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁהָיוּ הָעֶשֶׂר מַכּוֹת שֶׁל מִצְרַיִם
just as the ten plagues of Egypt
עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁנִּדְרָשׁ בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב לו, א)
in the manner expounded in the holy Zohar (Zohar II 36a):
they were clarified in one attribute
and went out of one kelipah,
in the attribute corresponding to it.
"and all … shall come upon you, etc.,
and pursue you and overtake you" (Devarim 28:45);
and not be ruined, Heaven forfend,
but that it will be assistance for good,
to bring them back in teshuvah.
and it is written "and pursue you,"
which is not written at the beginning of the passage.
they will accept the opposite with love;
but after the ten expressions pass,
which correspond to the ten attributes,
and the completion of the rectification is not yet,
that is, they will still be sunk
that they will be pursued by them,
שֶׁלֹּא יִרְצוּ לְקַבְּלָם בְּאַהֲבָה כָּל כָּךְ
so that they will not wish to accept them with love so much;
that you will not change through the opposite,
though these cause a person to transgress
against his own mind and the mind of his Maker
they will return through this in teshuvah.

p: מִן אֲשֶׁר יְשַׁלְּחֶנּוּ ה׳ בָּךְ וְגוֹמֵר (דְּבָרִים כח, מח)
from "whom Hashem will send against you, etc." (Devarim 28:48),
in which it is mentioned that Hashem will do;
and this is to rectify what they damaged
in the seven attributes of the structure.
וּכְתִיב וְהָיָה כַּאֲשֶׁר שָׂשׂ ה׳ וְגוֹמֵר
And it is written, "And it shall be, as Hashem rejoiced, etc.,
so Hashem will rejoice over you, etc.,
for in the decree of Haman,
כֵּן יַעֲמוֹד זַרְעֲכֶם וְשִׁמְכֶם (יְשַׁעְיָה סו, כב)
"so shall your seed and your name endure" (Yeshayahu 66:22).
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר חָדָשׁ (זֹהַר חָדָשׁ תָּבוֹא)
And as written in the Zohar Chadash (Zohar Chadash, Ki Savo)
גַּם כָּל חֳלִי וְכָל מַכָּה וְגוֹמֵר (דְּבָרִים כח, סא)
"Also every sickness and every plague, etc." (Devarim 28:61);
He will suppress them and cover them
so that they not come out, etc.;
the expression is mentioned several times,
"until He has destroyed," "until He has annihilated";
"so Hashem will rejoice to destroy and to annihilate,"
just as was the decree of Haman
כֵּיוָן שֶׁגְּזֵירָה כָּזוֹ לֹא יוּכַל לִהְיוֹת
since such a decree cannot be,
certainly it was decreed to be
that it will be for salvation.
in which it says that Hashem will do,
it is written, "And Hashem will bring you back in ships,"
שֶׁזֶּה נִדְרָשׁ בַּזֹּהַר חָדָשׁ (זֹהַר חָדָשׁ תָּבוֹא)
which is expounded in the Zohar Chadash (Zohar Chadash, Ki Savo)
as referring to the salvation and redemption at the end,
that Hashem, may He be blessed, will bring us back,
And Shabbos includes all seven attributes
וְאִיתָא בְּרַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא (חֵלֶק ג רנז, א)
and it is brought in Raya Mehemna (Zohar III 257a):
and she is the daughter, fourth to them."
And Shabbos includes all ten attributes;
and therefore they read this parshah on Shabbos,
for through keeping Shabbos according to its law
that although in the Gemara (Shabbos 118b) it is brought,
they merit, through the first Shabbos,
as is brought in several places

p: "And there you shall offer yourselves for sale, etc.,
and there will be no buyer";
and it says in the Zohar Chadash (Zohar Chadash, Ki Savo):
"'And you shall be sold' is not written,
but 'you shall offer yourselves for sale'
in your heart you will think
for 'there will be no buyer' is written, etc."
And according to what was said above,
that the pasuk "And Hashem will bring you back to Egypt, etc."
when Hashem will return the dispersed of Yisrael,
and "as in the days of your going out of Egypt
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר חָדָשׁ (זֹהַר חָדָשׁ תָּבוֹא)
and as written in the Zohar Chadash (Zohar Chadash, Ki Savo),
and it is written there "in the ships of their song"
just as there it is song,
so here too it is song,
how is it fitting to write afterward,
"and you shall offer yourselves for sale, etc.,"
that "you will think that you are sold,"
when it is speaking of after the redemption?
the most hidden of all hidden,
דְּאִיקְּרֵי אַיִן (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב סד, ב)
this is the mazal of Yisrael.
And so the verse says here,
when there will be "And Hashem will bring you back, etc.,"
"And there you shall offer yourselves for sale to your enemies
that is, that even at the time
that they were sold in exile
and it was not in their power
that they had been sold to the nations of the world
that they thought they had been sold
to the nations of the world;
but in truth it is not so,
for "and there will be no buyer" is written
that is, that the attribute of Ayin,
which is the aspect of Atika,
And this is according to what is brought in the Midrash
וְחֹשֶׁךְ עַל פְּנֵי תְהוֹם (בְּרֵאשִׁית א, ב)
and darkness upon the face of the deep" (Bereishis 1:2) is expounded
as referring to the four kingdoms;
that is, that in the utterance "Bereishis,"
which corresponds to the attribute of Atika,
so that from all this there would be
כִּדְאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב קפד, א)
as is brought in the holy Zohar (Zohar II 184a):
but that which comes out of darkness,
but that which comes out of evil."
may the memory of the tzaddik be a blessing, said,
that he heard from the Rebbe, Reb Bunim,
may the memory of the tzaddik be a blessing,
that although the minds of the generations
yet the point in the heart
And afterward I heard from our holy Rebbe
that he saw the matter stated explicitly
that is, in this orphaned generation,
when there is in the heart some true illumination,
it is more precious before Hashem, may He be blessed,
for according to the smallness of the minds
"For more are the children of the desolate
than the children of the married one" (Yeshayahu 54:1).
And likewise those who were sold
what they remember of Hashem, may He be blessed,
is precious to Hashem, may He be blessed,
in alluding to the four kingdoms
And this is the meaning of "and there will be no buyer":
that in truth the attribute of Ayin
